This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is stored as a literal entity-encoded string in the WordPress display_name field, which esc_html() passes through without re-encoding due to its double_encode=false behavior, allowing the browser to decode it to raw markup before the JavaScript sink consumes it.

items.title: A **server-side request forgery** flaw has been found in the get_remote_artifact_url() function in pulp_python/app/models.py of…
items.ai: CVSS 10.0（严重）。暂无公开 POC，按常规补丁窗口安排。 影响版本：详见公告。
items.desc: A **server-side request forgery** flaw has been found in the get_remote_artifact_url() function in pulp_python/app/models.py of the pull-through caching feature in the **pulp_python** package. The function uses the redirect query parameter from the client request as the URL to download. A network attacker or user who can reach the content app of a Python distribution that has a remote can choose that URL. The content app downloads it and returns the response. When the remote has a username and password, the download sends those credentials to the host in the URL. When the remote policy is immediate, the default, or on_demand, the file is saved into the distribution's repository and later clients are served that file. The project name and version come from the file, and the filename comes from the request path. A filename the repository already stores is served from the stored file.
